title_en: Stories of Modern China (14/20): Coming Home to Say Goodbye
note_en: The particle 过 after a verb marks something that has happened at least once, without saying when: 父亲年轻时帮大伯盖过房子 "her father had once helped her uncle build his house." With a negative it means "never (once)": 从来没有真正离开过这个大家庭 "she had never really left this big family." English uses "have ever / have never" or "once" for the same idea.
